pricing.recommendedModelRationale: IaaS is the recommended model for Peerless for five compounding reasons: (1) ComputerEase is Deltek-classified legacy with a 4-hour minimum support SLA and CE Live Service relay plumbing — ongoing monitoring and incident response have continuous operational value, not one-time build value. (2) MuleSoft IDP requires a manual-review queue and rule-library tuning as new contract templates appear or HD-side document formats shift — that is operational work, not implementation work. (3) Peerless has no in-house MuleSoft developer; Brian Cook is the Elevate platform IT director but has explicitly stated he is not the integration owner — he is in to debug GCP, not to operate integration flows. (4) Akoya is a PE sponsor actively hunting another Home Services platform — a managed-service relationship gives DataSkate continuous touchpoints during the 18-month window President Roger Greenhagel uses to modernize IT, positioning DataSkate for the next Akoya platform play. (5) The Elevate Fence Partners national-rollout thesis means UC1–UC4 are the template for 5 additional sibling brands — that template needs ongoing maintenance as state-specific rules (Wisconsin 99% deposit becomes N state exceptions) accumulate. Implementation Only would treat this as a one-time build and forfeit the recurring template-evolution role.
edgeCases: Flow count is 4 — sits at the top of the 1–5 retainer band. If Peerless promotes UC5 (deposit-paid) and UC6 (subcontract worksheet) to confirmed in a Phase 1b expansion, retainer jumps to the 6–10 band and 2-year total scales linearly.

At 4 flows, IaaS Year 1 ≈ Implementation Only flat fee — IaaS only wins on Year 2+. Implementation Only is the right fit only if Peerless hires a MuleSoft developer before kickoff. They have not signaled this.
Anypoint license bundling: the '$0 implementation when AE sells full Anypoint license' path is not in play at Peerless — no Anypoint license sale was discussed in scoping.
